newsitem.title: UKRAINE: New Ukraine economy minister condemns tax system.
newsitem.headline: New Ukraine economy minister condemns tax system.

text.p: Ukraine's newly-appointed economy minister on Tuesday condemned the tax collection system as ineffective and blamed parliamentary deputies for blocking efforts to create one that would work.

Yuri Yekhanurov, former chairman of the State Property Fund, told leading economists that Ukraine lost two billion hryvnia in uncollected tax revenues after the Tax Administration wrote off tax debts 216,000 times last year.
"I wish we had fewer illusions about the repayment of taxes," Yekhanurov said in his first public statement since taking the job late last month.
"There is a parliamentary lobby working in parliament to prevent normal tax collection," he said of delays by parliament to pass a new tax reform package.
Yekhanurov said the tax administration's one option is to pursue collection through courts, but said the arbitration court had only ruled on 1,004 cases last year.
Parliament, dominated by conservative deputies, is expected to pass this month or in April the tax reform package, on which the 1997 budget -- also awaiting approval -- will be based.

Ukraine's current tax system, which in some cases can tax up to 110 percent of profits, has been blamed as part of the reason for the huge shadow economy -- estimated to take up about 50 percent of all economic activity.
